0How to work a problem

Six named steps for every calculation

Each problem in this tutorial is worked in named steps. The names tell you what the step is for, so you can use the same pattern on new problems.

  1. Read and sketch. Draw the mechanism or system and mark what moves.
  2. List the data. Write each given value with its symbol and unit. The "Given" table on each problem does this for you.
  3. Convert to SI units. Millimetres to metres, rpm to rad/s, kN to N, degrees to radians where a formula needs them.
  4. Choose the relation. Name the law or formula and say why it applies.
  5. Substitute and work out. Put the numbers in, one quantity at a time, keeping three or four significant figures.
  6. Check and state the answer. Check the units and whether the size is sensible, then give the answer with its unit and direction.

Problem 1.1 Degrees of freedom of a six-link mechanism

A plane mechanism has six links, the frame included, joined by seven pin joints and no cam or gear contacts. Find its degrees of freedom and say what they mean.

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Links, frame includedNNN6
Lower pairs (pin joints)J1J_1J1​7
Higher pairsJ2J_2J2​0

Find

  • Degrees of freedom FFF
  • What kind of assembly it is

Terms used in this problem

Link
one rigid part; the fixed frame counts as a link.
Lower pair
a joint with surface contact (pin or slider); it leaves 1 freedom and removes 2.
Higher pair
a joint with point or line contact (cam, gear teeth); it removes 1 freedom.
Degrees of freedom FFF
the number of independent inputs needed to fix the position of every link.
Grübler and Kutzbach criterion
for plane mechanisms F=3(N−1)−2J1−J2F = 3(N-1) - 2J_1 - J_2F=3(N−1)−2J1​−J2​: three freedoms per moving link, less those the joints take away.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the freedom before joining

    Each of the N−1N - 1N−1 moving links could slide two ways and turn.

    3(N−1)=3×5=153(N-1) = 3 \times 5 = 153(N−1)=3×5=15
  2. Step 2Subtract the lower pairs
    2J1=2×7=142J_1 = 2 \times 7 = 142J1​=2×7=14
  3. Step 3Subtract the higher pairs
    J2=0J_2 = 0J2​=0
  4. Step 4Find the degrees of freedom
    F=15−14−0=1F = 15 - 14 - 0 = 1F=15−14−0=1
  5. Step 5Read the result

    F=1F = 1F=1: a constrained mechanism. One input fixes the motion of every link.

Answer F=1F = 1F=1, a constrained mechanism.

The same counts in a spatial linkage would give 6(N−1)−5J1−4J2=−56(N-1) - 5J_1 - 4J_2 = -56(N−1)−5J1​−4J2​=−5; the plane formula only applies to plane mechanisms.

Problem 1.2 A ball thrown from a height

A ball leaves a hand 1.5 m above level ground at 20 m/s, 35° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, find the highest point, the time of flight and the horizontal range.

Course practice question

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Launch speedvvv20 m/s
Launch angleθ\thetaθ35°
Launch heighty0y_0y0​1.5 m
Gravityggg9.81 m/s²

Find

  • Greatest height yyy
  • Time of flight ttt
  • Range xxx

Terms used in this problem

Projectile
a body moving freely under gravity alone once released.
Components
the velocity split into a horizontal part (vx)0(v_x)_0(vx​)0​ and a vertical part (vy)0(v_y)_0(vy​)0​.
Horizontal motion
no force acts sideways, so vxv_xvx​ stays constant.
Vertical motion
constant downward acceleration ggg, so vy2=(vy)02−2g(y−y0)v_y^2 = (v_y)_0^2 - 2g(y - y_0)vy2​=(vy​)02​−2g(y−y0​) and y=y0+(vy)0t−12gt2y = y_0 + (v_y)_0 t - \tfrac12 g t^2y=y0​+(vy​)0​t−21​gt2.

Solution

  1. Step 1Split the velocity
    (vx)0=20cos⁡35∘=16.38 m/s,(vy)0=20sin⁡35∘=11.47 m/s(v_x)_0 = 20\cos 35^\circ = 16.38\ \text{m/s},\qquad (v_y)_0 = 20\sin 35^\circ = 11.47\ \text{m/s}(vx​)0​=20cos35∘=16.38 m/s,(vy​)0​=20sin35∘=11.47 m/s
  2. Step 2Find the highest point

    At the top the vertical velocity is zero.

    y=y0+(vy)022g=1.5+11.4722×9.81=8.21 my = y_0 + \frac{(v_y)_0^2}{2g} = 1.5 + \frac{11.47^2}{2 \times 9.81} = 8.21\ \text{m}y=y0​+2g(vy​)02​​=1.5+2×9.8111.472​=8.21 m
  3. Step 3Find the time of flight

    The ball lands when y=0y = 0y=0; take the positive root of the quadratic.

    t=(vy)0+(vy)02+2gy0g=11.47+131.6+29.49.81=2.46 st = \frac{(v_y)_0 + \sqrt{(v_y)_0^2 + 2g y_0}}{g} = \frac{11.47 + \sqrt{131.6 + 29.4}}{9.81} = 2.46\ \text{s}t=g(vy​)0​+(vy​)02​+2gy0​​​=9.8111.47+131.6+29.4​​=2.46 s
  4. Step 4Find the range
    x=(vx)0 t=16.38×2.463=40.4 mx = (v_x)_0\, t = 16.38 \times 2.463 = 40.4\ \text{m}x=(vx​)0​t=16.38×2.463=40.4 m

Answer Highest point 8.21 m above the ground; flight 2.46 s; range 40.4 m.

Short problems

1.AThree links are pinned into a triangle. Find the degrees of freedom.

Term: Structure: an assembly with no relative motion.

  1. Step 1Apply the criterion
    F=3(3−1)−2×3=0F = 3(3-1) - 2 \times 3 = 0F=3(3−1)−2×3=0

Answer F=0F = 0F=0: a structure, nothing can move.

1.BA 0.2 kg mass whirls at 2 m/s on a 0.5 m string. Find the string tension.

Term: Centripetal force: the inward force that keeps a mass on a circle.

  1. Step 1Use the centripetal force
    F=mv2r=0.2×220.5=1.6 NF = \frac{m v^2}{r} = \frac{0.2 \times 2^2}{0.5} = 1.6\ \text{N}F=rmv2​=0.50.2×22​=1.6 N

Answer 1.6 N, pulling the mass inwards.

Problem 2.1 Kutzbach criterion for five linkages

Find the degrees of freedom of these plane linkages, given links lll, binary joints jjj and higher pairs hhh, and say what each is: (a) 3, 3, 0; (b) 4, 4, 0; (c) 5, 5, 0; (d) 5, 6, 0; (e) 6, 8, 0.

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
(a) trianglel,j,hl, j, hl,j,h3, 3, 0
(b) four-barl,j,hl, j, hl,j,h4, 4, 0
(c) five-barl,j,hl, j, hl,j,h5, 5, 0
(d)l,j,hl, j, hl,j,h5, 6, 0
(e)l,j,hl, j, hl,j,h6, 8, 0

Find

  • Degrees of freedom nnn for each
  • Type of assembly

Terms used in this problem

Binary joint
a pin joining exactly two links. A pin joining kkk links counts as k−1k - 1k−1 binary joints.
Kutzbach criterion
n=3(l−1)−2j−hn = 3(l - 1) - 2j - hn=3(l−1)−2j−h for plane linkages.
Reading nnn
n=1n = 1n=1 constrained mechanism; n=2n = 2n=2 needs two inputs; n=0n = 0n=0 structure; n<0n < 0n<0 a structure with redundant members (statically indeterminate).

Solution

  1. Step 1Write the criterion
    n=3(l−1)−2j−hn = 3(l - 1) - 2j - hn=3(l−1)−2j−h
  2. Step 2Work out (a) and (b)
    (a) 3(2)−6=0,(b) 3(3)−8=1(a)\ 3(2) - 6 = 0,\qquad (b)\ 3(3) - 8 = 1(a) 3(2)−6=0,(b) 3(3)−8=1
  3. Step 3Work out (c) and (d)
    (c) 3(4)−10=2,(d) 3(4)−12=0(c)\ 3(4) - 10 = 2,\qquad (d)\ 3(4) - 12 = 0(c) 3(4)−10=2,(d) 3(4)−12=0
  4. Step 4Work out (e)
    (e) 3(5)−16=−1(e)\ 3(5) - 16 = -1(e) 3(5)−16=−1
  5. Step 5Name each assembly

    (a) structure; (b) constrained mechanism; (c) needs two inputs; (d) structure; (e) statically indeterminate structure.

Answer (a) 0, (b) 1, (c) 2, (d) 0, (e) −1.

Problem 2.2 Crank and slotted-lever quick return

In a crank and slotted-lever quick-return mechanism the fixed centres are 240 mm apart and the driving crank is 120 mm long. Find the inclination of the slotted bar to the vertical at its extreme position, and the ratio of cutting time to return time. If the slotted bar is 450 mm long, find the stroke, the line of stroke passing through the extreme positions of the free end of the lever.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 5.2

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Distance between fixed centresACACAC240 mm
Crank lengthCB1CB_1CB1​120 mm
Slotted bar lengthAP1AP_1AP1​450 mm

Find

  • Inclination of the bar
  • Time ratio
  • Stroke R1R2R_1R_2R1​R2​

Terms used in this problem

Quick-return mechanism
a mechanism whose forward (cutting) stroke takes longer than the return, as in a shaping machine.
Slotted lever
the bar pivoted at AAA with a slot in which the crank pin slides.
Extreme position
where the slotted lever is tangent to the crank-pin circle: crank and lever are at 90°.
Angle α\alphaα
the angle the crank turns through during the return stroke.
Time ratio
cutting time over return time, (360∘−α)/α(360^\circ - \alpha)/\alpha(360∘−α)/α, for a crank at steady speed.

Solution

  1. Step 1Use the right angle at the extreme position

    Triangle AB1CAB_1CAB1​C has its right angle at B1B_1B1​.

    sin⁡∠CAB1=CB1AC=120240=0.5,∠CAB1=30∘\sin\angle CAB_1 = \frac{CB_1}{AC} = \frac{120}{240} = 0.5,\qquad \angle CAB_1 = 30^\circsin∠CAB1​=ACCB1​​=240120​=0.5,∠CAB1​=30∘
  2. Step 2Find the return angle

    The angle at CCC is 90∘−30∘=60∘=α/290^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ = \alpha/290∘−30∘=60∘=α/2.

    α=120∘\alpha = 120^\circα=120∘
  3. Step 3Find the time ratio
    360∘−αα=240120=2\frac{360^\circ - \alpha}{\alpha} = \frac{240}{120} = 2α360∘−α​=120240​=2
  4. Step 4Find the stroke

    The free end swings 30∘30^\circ30∘ each side of the vertical.

    R1R2=2 AP1sin⁡30∘=2×450×0.5=450 mmR_1R_2 = 2\,AP_1\sin 30^\circ = 2 \times 450 \times 0.5 = 450\ \text{mm}R1​R2​=2AP1​sin30∘=2×450×0.5=450 mm

Answer Bar inclined at 30° to the vertical; time ratio 2; stroke 450 mm.

Problem 2.3 Designing an oscillating-link quick return

A quick-return mechanism of the oscillating-link type has a driving crank BC 30 mm long. The ratio of working-stroke time to return time is to be 1.7, and the working stroke of R is 120 mm. Find the lengths AC and AP.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 5.3

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
CrankBCBCBC30 mm
Time ratiokkk1.7
StrokeR1R2R_1R_2R1​R2​120 mm

Find

  • Distance between centres ACACAC
  • Lever length APAPAP

Terms used in this problem

Oscillating link
the slotted lever that swings to and fro about AAA.
Time ratio kkk
(360∘−α)/α(360^\circ - \alpha)/\alpha(360∘−α)/α, where α\alphaα is the crank angle for the return stroke.
Stroke
the distance the tool end RRR travels from one extreme to the other.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the return angle
    k=360∘−αα ⇒ α=360∘k+1=3602.7=133.3∘k = \frac{360^\circ - \alpha}{\alpha}\ \Rightarrow\ \alpha = \frac{360^\circ}{k + 1} = \frac{360}{2.7} = 133.3^\circk=α360∘−α​ ⇒ α=k+1360∘​=2.7360​=133.3∘
  2. Step 2Find half the angle
    α2=66.67∘\frac{\alpha}{2} = 66.67^\circ2α​=66.67∘
  3. Step 3Find the distance between centres

    Right angle at B1B_1B1​ again, with sin⁡(90∘−α/2)=BC/AC\sin(90^\circ - \alpha/2) = BC/ACsin(90∘−α/2)=BC/AC.

    AC=BCcos⁡(α/2)=30cos⁡66.67∘=75.7 mmAC = \frac{BC}{\cos(\alpha/2)} = \frac{30}{\cos 66.67^\circ} = 75.7\ \text{mm}AC=cos(α/2)BC​=cos66.67∘30​=75.7 mm
  4. Step 4Find the lever length

    The stroke is the chord swept by PPP: L=2APcos⁡(α/2)L = 2AP\cos(\alpha/2)L=2APcos(α/2).

    AP=L2cos⁡(α/2)=1202×0.3961=151.5 mmAP = \frac{L}{2\cos(\alpha/2)} = \frac{120}{2 \times 0.3961} = 151.5\ \text{mm}AP=2cos(α/2)L​=2×0.3961120​=151.5 mm

Answer AC=75.7AC = 75.7AC=75.7 mm and AP=151.5AP = 151.5AP=151.5 mm.

Short problems

2.AA chain has l=5l = 5l=5 links and j=5j = 5j=5 joints. Using j=32l−2j = \tfrac32 l - 2j=23​l−2, what kind of chain is it?

Term: Kinematic chain: one in which each link moves in a definite way.

  1. Step 1Find the joints a kinematic chain needs
    32×5−2=5.5\tfrac32 \times 5 - 2 = 5.523​×5−2=5.5
  2. Step 2Compare
    j=5<5.5j = 5 < 5.5j=5<5.5

Answer An unconstrained chain.

2.BFour links meet at one pin. How many binary joints is that equivalent to?

Term: Quaternary joint: a pin shared by four links.

  1. Step 1Count k−1k - 1k−1
    4−1=34 - 1 = 34−1=3

Answer 3 binary joints.

2.CA four-bar has links 40, 75, 100 and 110 mm. Does it obey Grashof's law, and which link must be fixed for a double crank?

Term: Grashof's law: if s+l≤p+qs + l \le p + qs+l≤p+q, at least one link can turn fully.

  1. Step 1Compare shortest plus longest with the other two
    s+l=40+110=150≤p+q=75+100=175s + l = 40 + 110 = 150 \le p + q = 75 + 100 = 175s+l=40+110=150≤p+q=75+100=175

Answer Yes; fix the 40 mm link.

2.DIn a crank and slotted-lever quick return, AC=200AC = 200AC=200 mm and CB=100CB = 100CB=100 mm. Find the time ratio.

  1. Step 1Find α\alphaα
    cos⁡α2=100200,α2=60∘,α=120∘\cos\frac{\alpha}{2} = \frac{100}{200},\quad \frac{\alpha}{2} = 60^\circ,\quad \alpha = 120^\circcos2α​=200100​,2α​=60∘,α=120∘
  2. Step 2Find the ratio
    360−120120=2\frac{360 - 120}{120} = 2120360−120​=2

Answer Time ratio 2.

2.ETwo shafts 20 mm apart are joined by an Oldham's coupling turning at 10 rad/s. Find the greatest sliding speed of a tongue.

Term: Oldham's coupling: joins two parallel shafts that are slightly offset.

  1. Step 1Sliding speed
    v=rω=0.02×10=0.2 m/sv = r\omega = 0.02 \times 10 = 0.2\ \text{m/s}v=rω=0.02×10=0.2 m/s

Answer 0.2 m/s.

Problem 3.2 Output speed of a four-bar by the velocity diagram

In a four-bar chain ABCD, AD is fixed and 150 mm long. The crank AB is 40 mm long and turns at 120 rpm clockwise, while CD=80CD = 80CD=80 mm oscillates about D. BC and AD are equal. Find the angular velocity of CD when angle BAD=60∘BAD = 60^\circBAD=60∘.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 7.1

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
FrameADADAD150 mm
CrankABABAB40 mm
CouplerBCBCBC150 mm
OutputCDCDCD80 mm
Crank angle∠BAD\angle BAD∠BAD60°
Crank speedNNN120 rpm clockwise

Find

  • Angular velocity ωCD\omega_{CD}ωCD​

Terms used in this problem

Velocity diagram
a vector drawing of velocities from a pole aaa (fixed points); a lower-case letter is the image of the point with that capital letter.
Relative velocity
for two points on one rigid link, vBAv_{BA}vBA​ is perpendicular to ABABAB and equals ω×AB\omega \times ABω×AB.
Sine rule on the velocity triangle
the sides of the triangle are perpendicular to the links, so its angles equal the angles between the links.
Transmission angle γ\gammaγ
the angle between coupler and output link at CCC.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the crank speed and vBv_BvB​

    vBv_BvB​ is perpendicular to ABABAB.

    ωBA=2π×12060=12.57 rad/s,vB=12.57×0.04=0.503 m/s\omega_{BA} = \frac{2\pi \times 120}{60} = 12.57\ \text{rad/s},\qquad v_B = 12.57 \times 0.04 = 0.503\ \text{m/s}ωBA​=602π×120​=12.57 rad/s,vB​=12.57×0.04=0.503 m/s
  2. Step 2Fix the position

    Cosine rule for BDBDBD, then for the angle at CCC.

    BD2=402+1502−2(40)(150)cos⁡60∘=18 100,BD=134.5 mmBD^2 = 40^2 + 150^2 - 2(40)(150)\cos 60^\circ = 18\,100,\qquad BD = 134.5\ \text{mm}BD2=402+1502−2(40)(150)cos60∘=18100,BD=134.5 mm
    cos⁡γ=1502+802−18 1002(150)(80)=0.45,γ=63.26∘\cos\gamma = \frac{150^2 + 80^2 - 18\,100}{2(150)(80)} = 0.45,\qquad \gamma = 63.26^\circcosγ=2(150)(80)1502+802−18100​=0.45,γ=63.26∘
  3. Step 3Find the link directions

    From the coordinates of BBB and CCC: ABABAB at 60°, BCBCBC at 17.15°, DCDCDC at 80.41° to ADADAD.

Solution, continued

  1. Step 4Solve the velocity triangle

    vC=vB+vCBv_C = v_B + v_{CB}vC​=vB​+vCB​; the triangle angles are the angles between the links.

Problem 3.3 Steam-engine mechanism: velocities and rubbing

The crank and connecting rod of a steam engine are 0.5 m and 2 m long; the crank turns at 180 rpm clockwise. At 45° from inner dead centre, find the piston velocity, the angular velocity of the rod, the velocity of a point E on the rod 1.5 m from the gudgeon pin, the rubbing velocities at the crankshaft, crank-pin and cross-head pins (diameters 50, 60 and 30 mm), and the point G on the rod with the least velocity.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 7.2

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
CrankOB=rOB = rOB=r0.5 m

  • Point G of least velocity

Terms used in this problem

Inner dead centre (IDC)
the position with crank and rod in line and the piston nearest the crank.

n=l/rn = l/rn=l/r; here 4.
Velocity image
a point on a link has its image on the velocity diagram dividing the line in the same ratio.
Rubbing velocity
the speed at which pin and eye slide on each other: pin radius × relative angular velocity of the two links.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the crank speed and vBv_BvB​
    ω=2π×18060=18.85 rad/s,vB=18.85×0.5=9.425 m/s\omega = \frac{2\pi \times 180}{60} = 18.85\ \text{rad/s},\qquad v_B = 18.85 \times 0.5 = 9.425\ \text{m/s}ω=602π×180​=18.85 rad/s,vB​=18.85×0.5=9.425 m/s
  2. Step 2Find the piston velocity

    Exact form, with n2−sin⁡2θ=16−0.5=3.937\sqrt{n^2 - \sin^2\theta} = \sqrt{16 - 0.5} = 3.937n2−sin2θ​=16−0.5​=3.937.

    vP=ωr(sin⁡θ+sin⁡2θ2n2−sin⁡2θ)=9.425 (0.7071+0.1270)=7.86 m/sv_P = \omega r\left(\sin\theta + \frac{\sin 2\theta}{2\sqrt{n^2 - \sin^2\theta}}\right) = 9.425\,(0.7071 + 0.1270) = 7.86\ \text{m/s}vP​=ωr(sinθ+2n2−sin2θ​sin2θ​)=9.425(0.7071+0.1270)=7.86 m/s
  3. Step 3Find the rod angular velocity
    ωPB=ωcos⁡θn2−sin⁡2θ=18.85×0.70713.937=3.385 rad/s,vPB=6.771 m/s\omega_{PB} = \frac{\omega\cos\theta}{\sqrt{n^2 - \sin^2\theta}} = \frac{18.85 \times 0.7071}{3.937} = 3.385\ \text{rad/s},\qquad v_{PB} = 6.771\ \text{m/s}ωPB​=n2−sin2θ​ωcosθ​=3.93718.85×0.7071​=3.385 rad/s,vPB​=6.771 m/s

Solution, continued

  1. Step 4Find the velocity of E

    eee lies on bpbpbp with be=bp×BE/BPbe = bp \times BE/BPbe=bp×BE/BP; the angle between obobob and bpbpbp is 124.8°.

    be=6.771×0.52=1.693 m/sbe = 6.771 \times \frac{0.5}{2} = 1.693\ \text{m/s}be=6.771×20.5​=1.693 m/s
    vE=9.4252+1.6932+2(9.425)(1.693)cos⁡124.8∘=8.57 m/sv_E = \sqrt{9.425^2 + 1.693^2 + 2(9.425)(1.693)\cos 124.8^\circ} = 8.57\ \text{m/s}vE​=9.4252+1.6932+2(9.425)(1.693)cos124.8∘​=8.57 m/s

  3. Step 6Find the point of least velocity

    BG=l bgbp=2×5.386.771=1.59 mBG = l\,\frac{bg}{bp} = 2 \times \frac{5.38}{6.771} = 1.59\ \text{m}BG=lbpbg​=2×6.7715.38​=1.59 m

Short problems

3.AHow many instantaneous centres does a six-link mechanism have?

  1. Step 1Count
    N=6×52=15N = \frac{6 \times 5}{2} = 15N=26×5​=15

Answer 15.

3.BTwo links joined by a 40 mm pin turn at 5 rad/s clockwise and 3 rad/s anticlockwise. Find the rubbing velocity.

  1. Step 1Opposite senses add
    v=(ω1+ω2) r=8×0.02=0.16 m/sv = (\omega_1 + \omega_2)\,r = 8 \times 0.02 = 0.16\ \text{m/s}v=(ω1​+ω2​)r=8×0.02=0.16 m/s

Answer 0.16 m/s.

3.CIn a four-bar the input turns at 10 rad/s and the output at 4 rad/s. With 80% efficiency, find the actual mechanical advantage.

  1. Step 1Apply the definition
    M.A.=η ωAωB=0.8×104=2\text{M.A.} = \eta\,\frac{\omega_A}{\omega_B} = 0.8 \times \frac{10}{4} = 2M.A.=ηωB​ωA​​=0.8×410​=2

Answer 2.

3.DA rod BA of 0.5 m has aBAt=20a^t_{BA} = 20aBAt​=20 m/s². Find its angular acceleration.

  1. Step 1Divide by the length
    α=atAB=200.5=40 rad/s2\alpha = \frac{a^t}{AB} = \frac{20}{0.5} = 40\ \text{rad/s}^2α=ABat​=0.520​=40 rad/s2

Answer 40 rad/s².

Problem 4.1 Compound belt drive with slip

An engine at 150 rpm drives a line shaft by a belt. The engine pulley is 750 mm and the line-shaft pulley 450 mm in diameter. A 900 mm pulley on the line shaft drives a 150 mm pulley on a dynamo shaft. Find the dynamo speed (1) with no slip, (2) with 2% slip at each drive.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 11.1

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Engine speedN1N_1N1​150 rpm
Pulley diametersd1,d2,d3,d4d_1, d_2, d_3, d_4d1​,d2​,d3​,d4​750, 450, 900, 150 mm
Slip at each drivesss2%

Find

  • Dynamo speed N4N_4N4​, without and with slip

Terms used in this problem

Velocity ratio
with no slip the belt speed is the same on both pulleys, so N1d1=N2d2N_1 d_1 = N_2 d_2N1​d1​=N2​d2​.
Compound drive
two belts in series via a middle shaft carrying two pulleys; the ratios multiply.
Slip
the belt sliding on the pulley; s%s\%s% slip lowers the driven speed by that percentage.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the overall ratio
    N4N1=d1d3d2d4=750×900450×150=10\frac{N_4}{N_1} = \frac{d_1 d_3}{d_2 d_4} = \frac{750 \times 900}{450 \times 150} = 10N1​N4​​=d2​d4​d1​d3​​=450×150750×900​=10
  2. Step 2Find the speed without slip
    N4=150×10=1500 rpmN_4 = 150 \times 10 = 1500\ \text{rpm}N4​=150×10=1500 rpm
  3. Step 3Allow for slip at both drives
    N4=1500×(1−0.02)(1−0.02)=1440.6 rpmN_4 = 1500 \times (1 - 0.02)(1 - 0.02) = 1440.6\ \text{rpm}N4​=1500×(1−0.02)(1−0.02)=1440.6 rpm

Answer 1500 rpm without slip; 1441 rpm with 2% slip at each drive.

Problem 4.2 Speed lost to creep

A pulley 1 m in diameter at 200 rpm drives a pulley 2.25 m in diameter by a belt. Find the speed lost by the driven pulley through creep, if the stresses on the tight and slack sides are 1.4 MPa and 0.5 MPa and EEE for the belt is 100 MPa.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 11.2

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Driver diameter and speedd1,N1d_1, N_1d1​,N1​1 m, 200 rpm
Driven diameterd2d_2d2​2.25 m
Tight-side stressσ1\sigma_1σ1​1.4 MPa
Slack-side stressσ2\sigma_2σ2​0.5 MPa
Belt modulusEEE100 MPa

Find

  • Speed lost through creep

Terms used in this problem

Creep
the belt stretches more on the tight side than on the slack side, so it slowly crawls over the pulleys and the driven pulley falls behind.
Modulus EEE
the stiffness of the belt material: stress over strain.
Formula used
Khurmi and Gupta give N2/N1=(d1/d2)(E+σ2)/(E+σ1)N_2/N_1 = (d_1/d_2)(E + \sqrt{\sigma_2})/(E + \sqrt{\sigma_1})N2​/N1​=(d1​/d2​)(E+σ2​​)/(E+σ1​​), all in N/m².

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the speed without creep
    N2=200×12.25=88.8889 rpmN_2 = 200 \times \frac{1}{2.25} = 88.8889\ \text{rpm}N2​=200×2.251​=88.8889 rpm
  2. Step 2Find the square roots of the stresses

    In N/m².

    1.4×106=1183.2,0.5×106=707.1\sqrt{1.4 \times 10^6} = 1183.2,\qquad \sqrt{0.5 \times 10^6} = 707.11.4×106​=1183.2,0.5×106​=707.1
  3. Step 3Find the creep factor
    E+σ2E+σ1=100×106+707.1100×106+1183.2=0.99999524\frac{E + \sqrt{\sigma_2}}{E + \sqrt{\sigma_1}} = \frac{100 \times 10^6 + 707.1}{100 \times 10^6 + 1183.2} = 0.99999524E+σ1​​E+σ2​​​=100×106+1183.2100×106+707.1​=0.99999524
  4. Step 4Find the speed lost
    N2=88.8889×0.99999524=88.8885 rpm,lost 0.00042 rpmN_2 = 88.8889 \times 0.99999524 = 88.8885\ \text{rpm},\qquad \text{lost } 0.00042\ \text{rpm}N2​=88.8889×0.99999524=88.8885 rpm,lost 0.00042 rpm

Answer About 0.0004 rpm by the textbook formula.

The formula mixes EEE with σ\sqrt\sigmaσ​. Using the strains directly, (E+σ2)/(E+σ1)=100.5/101.4(E + \sigma_2)/(E + \sigma_1) = 100.5/101.4(E+σ2​)/(E+σ1​)=100.5/101.4, gives a loss of about 0.79 rpm; discuss which is physically sound.

Problem 4.3 Stepped (cone) pulleys

A shaft at a constant 160 rpm drives a parallel shaft 720 mm away, which has to run at 60, 80 and 100 rpm. The smallest pulley on the driving shaft is 40 mm in radius. Find the other radii of the two stepped pulleys for (1) a crossed belt, (2) an open belt. Neglect belt thickness and slip.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 11.3

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Driver speedN1=N3=N5N_1 = N_3 = N_5N1​=N3​=N5​160 rpm
Driven speedsN2,N4,N6N_2, N_4, N_6N2​,N4​,N6​60, 80, 100 rpm
Centre distancexxx720 mm
Smallest driver radiusr1r_1r1​40 mm

Find

  • Radii r2r_2r2​ to r6r_6r6​ for crossed and open belts

Terms used in this problem

Stepped pulleys
pulleys with several diameters side by side, so one belt can give several speeds.
Crossed belt length
L=π(r1+r2)+2x+(r1+r2)2/xL = \pi(r_1 + r_2) + 2x + (r_1 + r_2)^2/xL=π(r1​+r2​)+2x+(r1​+r2​)2/x; it depends only on r1+r2r_1 + r_2r1​+r2​.
Open belt length
L=π(r1+r2)+2x+(r2−r1)2/xL = \pi(r_1 + r_2) + 2x + (r_2 - r_1)^2/xL=π(r1​+r2​)+2x+(r2​−r1​)2/x.
Same belt on every step
the length must be the same for each pair of steps.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the first driven radius
    r2=r1N1N2=40×16060=106.7 mmr_2 = r_1\frac{N_1}{N_2} = 40 \times \frac{160}{60} = 106.7\ \text{mm}r2​=r1​N2​N1​​=40×60160​=106.7 mm
  2. Step 2Crossed belt: keep the sum

    Equal length means r3+r4=r5+r6=146.7r_3 + r_4 = r_5 + r_6 = 146.7r3​+r4​=r5​+r6​=146.7 mm.

    r4=2r3:r3=146.73=48.9,r4=97.8 mmr_4 = 2r_3:\quad r_3 = \frac{146.7}{3} = 48.9,\quad r_4 = 97.8\ \text{mm}r4​=2r3​:r3​=3146.7​=48.9,r4​=97.8 mm
    r6=1.6r5:r5=146.72.6=56.4,r6=90.3 mmr_6 = 1.6r_5:\quad r_5 = \frac{146.7}{2.6} = 56.4,\quad r_6 = 90.3\ \text{mm}r6​=1.6r5​:r5​=2.6146.7​=56.4,r6​=90.3 mm

Solution, continued

  1. Step 3Open belt: find the length
    L=π(146.7)+66.72720+2(720)=1906.9 mmL = \pi(146.7) + \frac{66.7^2}{720} + 2(720) = 1906.9\ \text{mm}L=π(146.7)+72066.72​+2(720)=1906.9 mm
  2. Step 4Open belt: solve for each step

    Put r4=2r3r_4 = 2r_3r4​=2r3​, then r6=1.6r5r_6 = 1.6r_5r6​=1.6r5​, into the same LLL and solve the quadratic.

    π(3r3)+r32720+1440=1906.9:r3=49.2,r4=98.4 mm\pi(3r_3) + \frac{r_3^2}{720} + 1440 = 1906.9:\quad r_3 = 49.2,\quad r_4 = 98.4\ \text{mm}π(3r3​)+720r32​​+1440=1906.9:r3​=49.2,r4​=98.4 mm
    π(2.6r5)+(0.6r5)2720+1440=1906.9:r5=57.0,r6=91.1 mm\pi(2.6r_5) + \frac{(0.6r_5)^2}{720} + 1440 = 1906.9:\quad r_5 = 57.0,\quad r_6 = 91.1\ \text{mm}π(2.6r5​)+720(0.6r5​)2​+1440=1906.9:r5​=57.0,r6​=91.1 mm

Answer Crossed: 106.7; 48.9 and 97.8; 56.4 and 90.3 mm. Open: 106.7; 49.2 and 98.4; 57.0 and 91.1 mm.

Problem 4.4 Power from the belt tensions

Find the power transmitted by a belt running over a pulley of 600 mm diameter at 200 rpm. The coefficient of friction is 0.25, the angle of lap 160° and the maximum tension 2500 N.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 11.4

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Pulley diameterddd0.6 m
SpeedNNN200 rpm
Friction coefficientμ\muμ0.25
Angle of lapθ\thetaθ160°
Maximum tensionT1T_1T1​2500 N

Find

  • Slack-side tension T2T_2T2​
  • Power PPP

Terms used in this problem

Tight and slack sides
the belt is pulled harder on the side going on to the driver (T1T_1T1​) than on the side leaving it (T2T_2T2​).
Angle of lap θ\thetaθ
the angle of contact between belt and pulley, in radians in the formulas.
Ratio of tensions
for a flat belt T1/T2=eμθT_1/T_2 = e^{\mu\theta}T1​/T2​=eμθ, often written 2.3log⁡(T1/T2)=μθ2.3\log(T_1/T_2) = \mu\theta2.3log(T1​/T2​)=μθ.
Power
P=(T1−T2) vP = (T_1 - T_2)\,vP=(T1​−T2​)v, the net pull times belt speed.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the belt speed
    v=πdN60=π×0.6×20060=6.283 m/sv = \frac{\pi d N}{60} = \frac{\pi \times 0.6 \times 200}{60} = 6.283\ \text{m/s}v=60πdN​=60π×0.6×200​=6.283 m/s
  2. Step 2Convert the angle of lap
    θ=160×π180=2.793 rad\theta = 160 \times \frac{\pi}{180} = 2.793\ \text{rad}θ=160×180π​=2.793 rad
  3. Step 3Find the ratio of tensions
    T1T2=eμθ=e0.25×2.793=e0.698=2.010\frac{T_1}{T_2} = e^{\mu\theta} = e^{0.25 \times 2.793} = e^{0.698} = 2.010T2​T1​​=eμθ=e0.25×2.793=e0.698=2.010
  4. Step 4Find the slack-side tension
    T2=25002.010=1244 NT_2 = \frac{2500}{2.010} = 1244\ \text{N}T2​=2.0102500​=1244 N
  5. Step 5Find the power
    P=(2500−1244)×6.283=7.89 kWP = (2500 - 1244) \times 6.283 = 7.89\ \text{kW}P=(2500−1244)×6.283=7.89 kW

Answer T2=1244T_2 = 1244T2​=1244 N; power 7.89 kW.

Two pulleys, 450 mm and 200 mm in diameter, are on parallel shafts 1.95 m apart, connected by a crossed belt. Find the belt length and the angle of contact on each pulley. What power can it carry when the larger pulley turns at 200 rpm, if the maximum tension is 1 kN and μ=0.25\mu = 0.25μ=0.25?

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Pulley radiir1,r2r_1, r_2r1​,r2​0.225 m, 0.1 m
Centre distancexxx1.95 m
Larger pulley speedN1N_1N1​200 rpm

Terms used in this problem

Tight and slack sides

the angle of contact between belt and pulley, in radians in the formulas.

    v=π×0.45×20060=4.712 m/sv = \frac{\pi \times 0.45 \times 200}{60} = 4.712\ \text{m/s}v=60π×0.45×200​=4.712 m/s

  3. Step 3Find the angle of contact
    sin⁡α=r1+r2x=0.1667,α=9.59∘,θ=180+2α=199.2∘=3.476 rad\sin\alpha = \frac{r_1 + r_2}{x} = 0.1667,\quad \alpha = 9.59^\circ,\qquad \theta = 180 + 2\alpha = 199.2^\circ = 3.476\ \text{rad}sinα=xr1​+r2​​=0.1667,α=9.59∘,θ=180+2α=199.2∘=3.476 rad

  5. Step 5Find the power

Problem 4.6 Greatest power of a flat belt

A pulley is driven by a flat belt with an angle of lap of 120°. The belt is 100 mm wide, 6 mm thick and of density 1000 kg/m³. If μ=0.3\mu = 0.3μ=0.3 and the stress must not exceed 2 MPa, find the greatest power the belt can carry and the belt speed for it.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 11.10

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Angle of lapθ\thetaθ120°
Width and thicknessb,tb, tb,t100 mm, 6 mm
Densityρ\rhoρ1000 kg/m³
Friction coefficientμ\muμ0.3
Allowable stressσ\sigmaσ2 MPa

Terms used in this problem

Tight and slack sides
the belt is pulled harder on the side going on to the driver (T1T_1T1​) than on the side leaving it (T2T_2T2​).
Angle of lap θ\thetaθ
the angle of contact between belt and pulley, in radians in the formulas.
Ratio of tensions
for a flat belt T1/T2=eμθT_1/T_2 = e^{\mu\theta}T1​/T2​=eμθ, often written 2.3log⁡(T1/T2)=μθ2.3\log(T_1/T_2) = \mu\theta2.3log(T1​/T2​)=μθ.
Power
P=(T1−T2) vP = (T_1 - T_2)\,vP=(T1​−T2​)v, the net pull times belt speed.
Centrifugal tension TCT_CTC​
mv2m v^2mv2, the extra tension caused by the belt whirling round the pulley; it carries no power.
Condition for greatest power
differentiating PPP with respect to vvv gives TC=T/3T_C = T/3TC​=T/3, so v=T/3mv = \sqrt{T/3m}v=T/3m​.

Solution

    T=σbt=2×106×0.1×0.006=1200 NT = \sigma b t = 2 \times 10^6 \times 0.1 \times 0.006 = 1200\ \text{N}T=σbt=2×106×0.1×0.006=1200 N
  2. Step 2Find the mass per metre
    m=btρ=0.1×0.006×1000=0.6 kg/mm = b t \rho = 0.1 \times 0.006 \times 1000 = 0.6\ \text{kg/m}m=btρ=0.1×0.006×1000=0.6 kg/m
  3. Step 3Find the speed for greatest power
    v=T3m=12001.8=25.82 m/sv = \sqrt{\frac{T}{3m}} = \sqrt{\frac{1200}{1.8}} = 25.82\ \text{m/s}v=3mT​​=1.81200​​=25.82 m/s

Solution, continued

  1. Step 4Find the tight-side tension
    TC=T3=400 N,T1=T−TC=800 NT_C = \frac{T}{3} = 400\ \text{N},\qquad T_1 = T - T_C = 800\ \text{N}TC​=3T​=400 N,T1​=T−TC​=800 N
  2. Step 5Find the slack-side tension
    T1T2=e0.3×2.094=1.874,T2=426.8 N\frac{T_1}{T_2} = e^{0.3 \times 2.094} = 1.874,\qquad T_2 = 426.8\ \text{N}T2​T1​​=e0.3×2.094=1.874,T2​=426.8 N
  3. Step 6Find the power
    P=(800−426.8)×25.82=9.64 kWP = (800 - 426.8) \times 25.82 = 9.64\ \text{kW}P=(800−426.8)×25.82=9.64 kW

Problem 4.7 Maximum power of a V-belt

A V-belt runs in a groove of included angle 30°. The belt is 20 mm deep and 20 mm wide at most, has a mass of 0.35 kg per metre and an allowable stress of 1.4 MPa. Find the maximum power when the angle of lap is 140° and μ=0.15\mu = 0.15μ=0.15.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 11.18

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Groove angle2β2\beta2β30°
Belt sectionb,tb, tb,t20 mm, 20 mm
Mass per metremmm0.35 kg/m
Allowable stressσ\sigmaσ1.4 MPa

Terms used in this problem

Tight and slack sides
the belt is pulled harder on the side going on to the driver (T1T_1T1​) than on the side leaving it (T2T_2T2​).
Angle of lap θ\thetaθ
the angle of contact between belt and pulley, in radians in the formulas.
Ratio of tensions
for a flat belt T1/T2=eμθT_1/T_2 = e^{\mu\theta}T1​/T2​=eμθ, often written 2.3log⁡(T1/T2)=μθ2.3\log(T_1/T_2) = \mu\theta2.3log(T1​/T2​)=μθ.
Power
P=(T1−T2) vP = (T_1 - T_2)\,vP=(T1​−T2​)v, the net pull times belt speed.
V-belt
a belt of wedge section running in a V-groove.
Wedge action
the groove sides press harder than the belt tension alone would, so the ratio becomes eμθ cosec βe^{\mu\theta\,\mathrm{cosec}\,\beta}eμθcosecβ.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the maximum tension
    T=σbt=1.4×106×0.02×0.02=560 NT = \sigma b t = 1.4 \times 10^6 \times 0.02 \times 0.02 = 560\ \text{N}T=σbt=1.4×106×0.02×0.02=560 N
  2. Step 2Find the speed for maximum power
    v=5603×0.35=23.09 m/sv = \sqrt{\frac{560}{3 \times 0.35}} = 23.09\ \text{m/s}v=3×0.35560​​=23.09 m/s
  3. Step 3Find the ratio of tensions
    μθ cosec β=0.15×2.443×1sin⁡15∘=1.416,T1T2=e1.416=4.121\mu\theta\,\mathrm{cosec}\,\beta = 0.15 \times 2.443 \times \frac{1}{\sin 15^\circ} = 1.416,\qquad \frac{T_1}{T_2} = e^{1.416} = 4.121μθcosecβ=0.15×2.443×sin15∘1​=1.416,T2​T1​​=e1.416=4.121
  4. Step 4Find the tensions
    TC=5603=186.7 N,T1=373.3 N,T2=373.34.121=90.6 NT_C = \frac{560}{3} = 186.7\ \text{N},\quad T_1 = 373.3\ \text{N},\quad T_2 = \frac{373.3}{4.121} = 90.6\ \text{N}TC​=3560​=186.7 N,T1​=373.3 N,T2​=4.121373.3​=90.6 N
  5. Step 5Find the power
    P=(373.3−90.6)×23.09=6.53 kWP = (373.3 - 90.6) \times 23.09 = 6.53\ \text{kW}P=(373.3−90.6)×23.09=6.53 kW

Answer Maximum power 6.53 kW.

4.DA belt may carry T=900T = 900T=900 N and has m=1m = 1m=1 kg/m. Find its speed for maximum power.

Answer 17.3 m/s.

4.EIf T1=1500T_1 = 1500T1​=1500 N and T2=500T_2 = 500T2​=500 N, find the initial tension, neglecting centrifugal tension.

Term: Initial tension: the tension in the belt at rest.

  1. Step 1Average the tensions
    T0=T1+T22=1000 NT_0 = \frac{T_1 + T_2}{2} = 1000\ \text{N}T0​=2T1​+T2​​=1000 N

Answer 1000 N.

Problem 5.1 Tooth load from power

A single-reduction gear of 120 kW has a pinion of 250 mm pitch-circle diameter running at 650 rpm. Find the total load on the teeth due to the power, the pressure angle being 20°.

  2. Step 2Find the torque
    T=Pω=120 00068.07=1763 N mT = \frac{P}{\omega} = \frac{120\,000}{68.07} = 1763\ \text{N m}T=ωP​=68.07120000​=1763 N m
  3. Step 3Find the tangential load
    FT=Tr=17630.125=14 104 NF_T = \frac{T}{r} = \frac{1763}{0.125} = 14\,104\ \text{N}FT​=rT​=0.1251763​=14104 N
  4. Step 4Find the radial and total loads
    FR=14 104tan⁡20∘=5133 N,F=14 104cos⁡20∘=15 009 NF_R = 14\,104\tan 20^\circ = 5133\ \text{N},\qquad F = \frac{14\,104}{\cos 20^\circ} = 15\,009\ \text{N}FR​=14104tan20∘=5133 N,F=cos20∘14104​=15009 N

Answer Total tooth load about 15.0 kN (tangential 14.1 kN, radial 5.13 kN).

Problem 5.2 Addendum from the arc of contact

Two equal spur gears in mesh have 40 teeth each, 20° involute profile and module 6 mm. If the arc of contact is 1.75 times the circular pitch, find the addendum.

    RA=(15.50+41.04)2+112.762=126.14 mmR_A = \sqrt{(15.50 + 41.04)^2 + 112.76^2} = 126.14\ \text{mm}RA​=(15.50+41.04)2+112.762​=126.14 mm

Problem 5.6 Fewest pinion teeth to avoid interference

Find the fewest teeth on a pinion, to avoid interference, which gears with (1) a wheel giving a ratio of 3 to 1, (2) an equal wheel. Pressure angle 20°, wheel addendum one module.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 12.9

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Gear ratioGGG3 (then 1)
Pressure angleϕ\phiϕ20°
Wheel addendumAwA_wAw​1 module

Find

  • Fewest pinion teeth in each case

Terms used in this problem

Interference
the tip of one tooth cutting into the root of the other below its base circle.
Formula
t=2AwG[1+1G(1G+2)sin⁡2ϕ−1]t = \dfrac{2A_w}{G\left[\sqrt{1 + \frac1G\left(\frac1G + 2\right)\sin^2\phi} - 1\right]}t=G[1+G1​(G1​+2)sin2ϕ​−1]2Aw​​, from keeping the wheel tip inside the interference point.
Rounding
teeth come in whole numbers, so always round up.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find sin⁡2ϕ\sin^2\phisin2ϕ
    sin⁡220∘=0.1170\sin^2 20^\circ = 0.1170sin220∘=0.1170
  2. Step 2Ratio 3: evaluate the bracket
    3[1+13×73×0.1170−1]=0.13353\left[\sqrt{1 + \tfrac13 \times \tfrac73 \times 0.1170} - 1\right] = 0.13353[1+31​×37​×0.1170​−1]=0.1335
  3. Step 3Ratio 3: find the teeth
    t=2×10.1335=14.98, so 15 teetht = \frac{2 \times 1}{0.1335} = 14.98,\ \text{so 15 teeth}t=0.13352×1​=14.98, so 15 teeth
  4. Step 4Equal wheel: put G=1G = 1G=1
    t=21+3×0.1170−1=12.32, so 13 teetht = \frac{2}{\sqrt{1 + 3 \times 0.1170} - 1} = 12.32,\ \text{so 13 teeth}t=1+3×0.1170​−12​=12.32, so 13 teeth

Answer 15 teeth for a 3 to 1 pair; 13 teeth with an equal wheel.

Problem 6.1 Knife-edge follower with uniform velocity

A cam gives a knife-edge follower an outstroke during 60° of cam rotation, a dwell for 30°, a return during 60° and a dwell for the remaining 210°. The stroke is 40 mm and the least radius of the cam 50 mm. The follower moves with uniform velocity both ways. Find the displacement step for drawing the profile, and the follower velocity at 100 rpm.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 20.1

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
StrokeSSS40 mm
Outstroke angleθO\theta_OθO​60°
Return angleθR\theta_RθR​60°
Cam speedNNN100 rpm

Find

  • Displacement per 10° of cam
  • Follower velocity

Terms used in this problem

Cam and follower
the cam is a shaped disc on a turning shaft; the follower rides on it and is pushed out and back.
Outstroke and return
the rise and the fall of the follower; θO\theta_OθO​ and θR\theta_RθR​ are the cam angles (radians in formulas) they take.
Stroke SSS
the total lift of the follower.
Dwell
a part of the turn during which the follower stays still.
Uniform velocity
the follower rises equal distances for equal cam angles: a straight-line displacement diagram.
Knife-edge follower
a follower with a sharp tip touching the cam.

Solution

  1. Step 1Divide the outstroke

    60° in six steps of 10°.

    S6=406=6.67 mm per division\frac{S}{6} = \frac{40}{6} = 6.67\ \text{mm per division}6S​=640​=6.67 mm per division
  2. Step 2Find the cam speed
    ω=2π×10060=10.47 rad/s\omega = \frac{2\pi \times 100}{60} = 10.47\ \text{rad/s}ω=602π×100​=10.47 rad/s
  3. Step 3Find the follower velocity

    Distance over time: the outstroke takes θO/ω\theta_O/\omegaθO​/ω.

    v=SωθO=0.04×10.47π/3=0.40 m/sv = \frac{S\omega}{\theta_O} = \frac{0.04 \times 10.47}{\pi/3} = 0.40\ \text{m/s}v=θO​Sω​=π/30.04×10.47​=0.40 m/s
  4. Step 4Check the acceleration

    The velocity jumps from zero to 0.40 m/s at once at each end.

    a is infinite at the start and end of each strokea\ \text{is infinite at the start and end of each stroke}a is infinite at the start and end of each stroke

Answer 6.67 mm per 10° of cam; 0.40 m/s at 100 rpm, with shocks at the ends of each stroke.

QuantitySymbolValue
StrokeSSS50 mm
Outstroke angleθO\theta_OθO​120°
Return angleθR\theta_RθR​60°
Cam speedNNN100 rpm

Find

  • Greatest velocity and acceleration on the outstroke and the return

Terms used in this problem

Cam and follower
the cam is a shaped disc on a turning shaft; the follower rides on it and is pushed out and back.
Outstroke and return
the rise and the fall of the follower; θO\theta_OθO​ and θR\theta_RθR​ are the cam angles (radians in formulas) they take.
Stroke SSS
the total lift of the follower.
Dwell
a part of the turn during which the follower stays still.
Simple harmonic motion (SHM)
the follower moves like the projection of a point going round a circle of diameter SSS; the displacement diagram is a half cosine wave.
Roller follower
a follower with a small wheel at its tip, which reduces wear.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the cam speed and angles
    ω=10.47 rad/s,θO=2π3=2.094,θR=π3=1.047 rad\omega = 10.47\ \text{rad/s},\qquad \theta_O = \frac{2\pi}{3} = 2.094,\qquad \theta_R = \frac{\pi}{3} = 1.047\ \text{rad}ω=10.47 rad/s,θO​=32π​=2.094,θR​=3π​=1.047 rad
  2. Step 2Find the greatest velocities

    At mid-stroke.

    vO=πωS2θO=0.393 m/s,vR=πωS2θR=0.785 m/sv_O = \frac{\pi\omega S}{2\theta_O} = 0.393\ \text{m/s},\qquad v_R = \frac{\pi\omega S}{2\theta_R} = 0.785\ \text{m/s}vO​=2θO​πωS​=0.393 m/s,vR​=2θR​πωS​=0.785 m/s
  3. Step 3Find the greatest accelerations

    At the ends of the stroke.

    aO=π2ω2S2θO2=6.17 m/s2,aR=π2ω2S2θR2=24.7 m/s2a_O = \frac{\pi^2\omega^2 S}{2\theta_O^2} = 6.17\ \text{m/s}^2,\qquad a_R = \frac{\pi^2\omega^2 S}{2\theta_R^2} = 24.7\ \text{m/s}^2aO​=2θO2​π2ω2S​=6.17 m/s2,aR​=2θR2​π2ω2S​=24.7 m/s2

Answer Velocity 0.393 m/s out and 0.785 m/s back; acceleration 6.17 m/s² out and 24.7 m/s² back.

Halving the angle for a stroke doubles the velocity and multiplies the acceleration by four.

Problem 6.3 Flat-faced follower with simple harmonic motion

A cam drives a flat reciprocating follower: during the first 120° the follower moves out 20 mm with SHM; it dwells for 30°; during the next 120° it moves back with SHM; it dwells for the last 90°. The least radius of the cam is 25 mm. Find how wide the follower face must be, and check that the profile stays convex.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 20.4

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
StrokeSSS20 mm
Outstroke angleθO\theta_OθO​120°
Least radiusRbR_bRb​25 mm

Find

  • Least face width
  • Smallest radius of curvature of the profile

Terms used in this problem

Cam and follower
the cam is a shaped disc on a turning shaft; the follower rides on it and is pushed out and back.
Outstroke and return
the rise and the fall of the follower; θO\theta_OθO​ and θR\theta_RθR​ are the cam angles (radians in formulas) they take.
Stroke SSS
the total lift of the follower.
Dwell
a part of the turn during which the follower stays still.
Flat-faced follower
a follower with a flat foot; the contact point moves across the face as the cam turns.
Offset of the contact point
equals ds/dθds/d\thetads/dθ, the slope of the displacement curve, so the face must be at least twice its largest value wide.
Radius of curvature
ρ=Rb+s+d2s/dθ2\rho = R_b + s + d^2s/d\theta^2ρ=Rb​+s+d2s/dθ2; it must stay positive or the profile would have a cusp.

Solution

  1. Step 1Write the SHM displacement
    s=S2(1−cos⁡πθθO)s = \frac{S}{2}\left(1 - \cos\frac{\pi\theta}{\theta_O}\right)s=2S​(1−cosθO​πθ​)
  2. Step 2Find the largest slope

    At mid-stroke.

    (dsdθ)max=πS2θO=π×202×2.094=15.0 mm\left(\frac{ds}{d\theta}\right)_{max} = \frac{\pi S}{2\theta_O} = \frac{\pi \times 20}{2 \times 2.094} = 15.0\ \text{mm}(dθds​)max​=2θO​πS​=2×2.094π×20​=15.0 mm
  3. Step 3Find the face width

    Contact moves 15 mm each side of the follower axis; add a margin.

    2×15=30 mm, so at least about 34 mm2 \times 15 = 30\ \text{mm, so at least about 34 mm}2×15=30 mm, so at least about 34 mm
  4. Step 4Find the smallest radius of curvature

    Most negative at the top of the stroke, where s=20s = 20s=20 and d2s/dθ2=−S2(π/θO)2=−22.5d^2s/d\theta^2 = -\tfrac{S}{2}(\pi/\theta_O)^2 = -22.5d2s/dθ2=−2S​(π/θO​)2=−22.5 mm.

    ρmin=25+20−22.5=22.5 mm>0\rho_{min} = 25 + 20 - 22.5 = 22.5\ \text{mm} > 0ρmin​=25+20−22.5=22.5 mm>0

Answer Face at least about 34 mm wide; smallest radius of curvature 22.5 mm, so the profile stays convex.

Problem 6.4 Uniform acceleration and retardation at high speed

A cam of least radius 50 mm, turning clockwise, gives a knife-edge follower an outstroke of 40 mm during 100°, a dwell of 80°, a return during 90° and a dwell for the remaining 90°. The motion is uniform acceleration and retardation. Find the greatest velocity and acceleration of the follower at 900 rpm.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 20.6

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
StrokeSSS40 mm
Outstroke angleθO\theta_OθO​100°
Return angleθR\theta_RθR​90°
Cam speedNNN900 rpm

Find

  • Greatest velocity and acceleration, out and back

Terms used in this problem

Cam and follower
the cam is a shaped disc on a turning shaft; the follower rides on it and is pushed out and back.
Outstroke and return
the rise and the fall of the follower; θO\theta_OθO​ and θR\theta_RθR​ are the cam angles (radians in formulas) they take.
Stroke SSS
the total lift of the follower.
Dwell
a part of the turn during which the follower stays still.
Uniform acceleration and retardation
the follower speeds up at a constant rate for half the stroke and slows down at the same rate for the other half; the displacement diagram is two parabolas.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the cam speed and angles
    ω=2π×90060=94.25 rad/s,θO=1.745,θR=1.571 rad\omega = \frac{2\pi \times 900}{60} = 94.25\ \text{rad/s},\qquad \theta_O = 1.745,\qquad \theta_R = 1.571\ \text{rad}ω=602π×900​=94.25 rad/s,θO​=1.745,θR​=1.571 rad
  2. Step 2Find the greatest velocities

    Reached half-way through each stroke.

    vO=2ωSθO=4.32 m/s,vR=2ωSθR=4.80 m/sv_O = \frac{2\omega S}{\theta_O} = 4.32\ \text{m/s},\qquad v_R = \frac{2\omega S}{\theta_R} = 4.80\ \text{m/s}vO​=θO​2ωS​=4.32 m/s,vR​=θR​2ωS​=4.80 m/s
  3. Step 3Find the accelerations

    Constant in each half.

    aO=4ω2SθO2=467 m/s2,aR=4ω2SθR2=576 m/s2a_O = \frac{4\omega^2 S}{\theta_O^2} = 467\ \text{m/s}^2,\qquad a_R = \frac{4\omega^2 S}{\theta_R^2} = 576\ \text{m/s}^2aO​=θO2​4ω2S​=467 m/s2,aR​=θR2​4ω2S​=576 m/s2

Answer Velocity 4.32 m/s out and 4.80 m/s back; acceleration 467 m/s² out and 576 m/s² back.

Problem 7.1 Four masses in one plane

Four masses of 200, 300, 240 and 260 kg rotate in one plane at radii 0.2, 0.15, 0.25 and 0.3 m. The angles between successive masses are 45°, 75° and 135°. Find the magnitude and position of the balance mass if its radius is 0.2 m.

Khurmi and Gupta (2020), Example 21.1

Given

QuantitySymbolValue
Massesm1,m2,m3,m4m_1, m_2, m_3, m_4m1​,m2​,m3​,m4​200, 300, 240, 260 kg
Radiir1,r2,r3,r4r_1, r_2, r_3, r_4r1​,r2​,r3​,r4​0.2, 0.15, 0.25, 0.3 m
Angles between successive masses45°, 75°, 135°
Balance-mass radiusrrr0.2 m

Find

  • Balance mass and its angle

Terms used in this problem

Centrifugal force
mω2rm\omega^2 rmω2r, the outward pull of a rotating mass; balancing makes these forces add to zero.
mrmrmr product
since every mass turns at the same ω\omegaω, only m×rm \times rm×r matters for balance.
Components
ΣH=Σmrcos⁡θ\Sigma H = \Sigma mr\cos\thetaΣH=Σmrcosθ and ΣV=Σmrsin⁡θ\Sigma V = \Sigma mr\sin\thetaΣV=Σmrsinθ, with angles from the first mass.
Balance mass
the extra mass placed opposite the resultant, so the total mrmrmr vector is zero.

Solution

  1. Step 1Find the angles from m1m_1m1​
    θ=0∘, 45∘, 120∘, 255∘\theta = 0^\circ,\ 45^\circ,\ 120^\circ,\ 255^\circθ=0∘, 45∘, 120∘, 255∘
  2. Step 2Find the mrmrmr products
    mr=40.0, 45.0, 60.0, 78.0 kg mmr = 40.0,\ 45.0,\ 60.0,\ 78.0\ \text{kg m}mr=40.0, 45.0, 60.0, 78.0 kg m
  3. Step 3Resolve horizontally and vertically
    ΣH=40+45cos⁡45∘+60cos⁡120∘+78cos⁡255∘=21.63 kg m\Sigma H = 40 + 45\cos 45^\circ + 60\cos 120^\circ + 78\cos 255^\circ = 21.63\ \text{kg m}ΣH=40+45cos45∘+60cos120∘+78cos255∘=21.63 kg m
    ΣV=45sin⁡45∘+60sin⁡120∘+78sin⁡255∘=8.44 kg m\Sigma V = 45\sin 45^\circ + 60\sin 120^\circ + 78\sin 255^\circ = 8.44\ \text{kg m}ΣV=45sin45∘+60sin120∘+78sin255∘=8.44 kg m
  4. Step 4Find the resultant
    R=21.632+8.442=23.22 kg mR = \sqrt{21.63^2 + 8.44^2} = 23.22\ \text{kg m}R=21.632+8.442​=23.22 kg m
  5. Step 5Find the balance mass and its angle

    It goes opposite the resultant.

    m=23.220.2=116.1 kg,tan⁡−18.4421.63=21.31∘,21.31+180=201.3∘m = \frac{23.22}{0.2} = 116.1\ \text{kg},\qquad \tan^{-1}\frac{8.44}{21.63} = 21.31^\circ,\qquad 21.31 + 180 = 201.3^\circm=0.223.22​=116.1 kg,tan−121.638.44​=21.31∘,21.31+180=201.3∘

Answer 116.1 kg at 201.3° from m1m_1m1​ (anticlockwise).

7.BWhat happens to the out-of-balance force if the speed doubles?

    F2F1=(2ωω)2=4\frac{F_2}{F_1} = \left(\frac{2\omega}{\omega}\right)^2 = 4F1​F2​​=(ω2ω​)2=4
